stories.title: Southwest-Inspired Cocktail Bar Setting Up Shop in South Street Seaport District
stories.excerpt: The Durst Organization announced that Mesa Bar, a new Southwestern-inspired cocktail and wine bar, has signed a lease at 220 Front St. in the South Street Seaport Historic District. Expected to open this year, Mesa will pair a creative cocktail program and curated wine list with cold beer and a concise menu of bar snacks in a setting shaped by founder and Upper West Side native Levent Cakir’s lifelong fascination with the American West. “Mesa Bar brings a fresh offering to Front Street and adds to the diverse mix of dining, retail, and hospitality experiences that make the block a special part of Lower Manhattan,” said Jody Durst, President of The Durst Organization. The Durst Organization was represented in-house by Karen Rose and by Zach Nathan, Brandon Berger, and Hunter Lazan of KSR. Mesa Bar was represented by Aynsley Thaler and David Green of KSR. The post Southwest-Inspired Cocktail Bar Setting Up Shop in South Street Seaport District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Mesa Bar signs lease at 220 Front St., South Street Seaport, Manhattan
Durst Organization landlord; new cocktail/wine bar opening 2025
Retail/hospitality activation in Lower Manhattan waterfront district
stories.summary: Mesa Bar, a Southwestern-inspired cocktail and wine bar, has leased space at 220 Front Street in the South Street Seaport Historic District from the Durst Organization, set to open this year. The venue will offer creative cocktails, curated wines, beer, and bar snacks. The deal signals continued confidence in Front Street's appeal as a mixed-use dining and hospitality destination in Lower Manhattan.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Retail/hospitality leasing activity indicates foot traffic demand and neighborhood vibrancy in Lower Manhattan, but does not directly signal residential demand drivers, supply constraints, or capital availability affecting apartment development in this market.

stories.title: Pegasus Completes Project Management for Two LA Retail Developments
stories.excerpt: Pegasus has completed project management engagements for two prominent retail developments: Raising Cane’s first location within the City of Los Angeles (Westwood Village) and a new Honey Baked Ham franchise in Sherman Oaks. Serving as the owner’s project management advisor, Pegasus helped guide each project from planning through completion. “Successful projects are built on thoughtful planning, clear communication, and disciplined execution,” said Mike McCanless, project manager. “Our responsibility is to help owners navigate the process from start to finish, coordinating the many moving parts so projects remain aligned with our clients’ objectives from the earliest stages of planning through project delivery.” The successful outcomes in Westwood Village and Sherman Oaks reflect the continued expansion of Pegasus’ construction and project management practice, which provides oversight throughout the development process, including entitlement coordination, budgeting and scheduling, consultant procurement, contractor management, construction loan administration, tenant coordination, and post-completion asset management. The post Pegasus Completes Project Management for Two LA Retail Developments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pegasus completed PM for Raising Cane's, Westwood Village; Honey Baked Ham, Sherman Oaks, LA
Project management firm guiding retail developments from planning through completion
QSR and franchise expansion in Los Angeles submarkets
stories.summary: Pegasus completed project management engagements for Raising Cane's first Los Angeles location in Westwood Village and a Honey Baked Ham franchise in Sherman Oaks. The firm served as owner's project management advisor through planning, entitlements, budgeting, contractor management, and post-completion. This reflects Pegasus' expanded construction and project management practice serving retail development.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. QSR and specialty retail expansion signals consumer foot traffic and neighborhood retail demand but does not address residential supply, job growth, or capital flows affecting apartment development feasibility in LA submarkets.

stories.title: Downtown Brooklyn Development Site Fetches $84M
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged the $83.5-million sale of the Bridge & Fulton Development Site, a large-scale mixed-use development opportunity located at 485 Fulton St. and 147 Lawrence St. in Downtown Brooklyn. Borough Developers acquired the property from ICER Real Estate. JLL’s Michael Mazzara, Ethan Stanton and Brendan Maddigan represented the seller and negotiated directly with the buyer. “This sale speaks to the continued strength of investor conviction in Downtown Brooklyn and, more broadly, the value developers are placing on well-located sites where they can build housing at meaningful scale,” said Mazzara. “There are very few opportunities of this size in a neighborhood with this level of transit access, residential demand and established retail.” Preliminary plans envision a four-building development comprising retail on the ground with residential above. The site is located within an Inner Transit Zone with no parking requirement and can benefit from additional development flexibility available through the City of Yes program. The post Downtown Brooklyn Development Site Fetches $84M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Borough Developers acquires Bridge & Fulton Development Site, Downtown Brooklyn, $83.5M
Mixed-use, four-building, ground-floor retail with residential above; no parking required
City of Yes zoning flexibility; high transit access; 485 Fulton St. and 147 Lawrence St.
stories.summary: Borough Developers acquired the Bridge & Fulton Development Site in Downtown Brooklyn for $83.5 million from ICER Real Estate, with JLL Capital Markets arranging the sale. The 485 Fulton Street and 147 Lawrence Street site is planned as a four-building mixed-use development with retail and residential components. The location benefits from an Inner Transit Zone with no parking requirement and City of Yes development flexibility.
stories.impact: Strong signal for Downtown Brooklyn multifamily market. Large-scale site sale at this price signals investor conviction and available capital for residential development; City of Yes zoning and transit proximity reduce entitlements friction and increase density/unit yield, making this submarket more competitive for new supply. Expect increased competition for adjacent sites and faster absorption if development moves forward.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Closes Multifamily Sale in San Diego’s College East
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of The Molokai Apartments, a 39-unit multifamily property in San Diego. The property sold for $11.2 million, or $287,179 per unit. “The property received a tremendous amount of attention from the investment community due in part to its spacious floor plans, which average more than 800 square feet and are significantly larger than the average units in the area,” said Austin Ray Huffman, senior director investments. “Buyers were also drawn to the property’s tenant amenities, including a private pool, secure access, storage and off-street parking.” Huffman and Chris Zorbas, of the Zorbas Huffman Group based out of Marcus & Millichap’s San Diego office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, Vista International, Inc. The buyer, a private investor, was represented by Michael Wolf of Coldwell Banker West. Built in 1971, The Molokai Apartments is a 32,204-square-foot property situated on 0.99 acres at 5055 73rd St. in San Diego’s College East neighborhood. The post Marcus & Millichap Closes Multifamily Sale in San Diego’s College East appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Molokai Apartments, 39-unit, sold $11.2M ($287K/unit) in College East, San Diego
Built 1971; 32,204 SF; spacious units (800+ SF avg); private pool, parking, storage
Strong buyer interest in older product with larger floor plans and amenities
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of The Molokai Apartments, a 39-unit property in San Diego's College East neighborhood, for $11.2 million ($287,179 per unit). The 1971-built property features spacious floor plans averaging over 800 square feet—significantly larger than area average—and amenities including a private pool, secure access, storage, and off-street parking. Strong investment community demand was attributed to unit size and amenity profile.
stories.impact: Modest relevance to multifamily development in San Diego. Unit price reflects investor appetite for established product with larger floor plans and tangible amenities; signals that aging stock with differentiated specs and quality can command competitive pricing. However, no new supply or demand catalyst disclosed; useful for comp analysis and renovation value-add thesis in San Diego's secondary neighborhoods.

stories.title: Rhone Signs 40K-SF Headquarters Lease with RFR in Stamford
stories.excerpt: Performance apparel brand Rhone has leased 40,000 square feet of office space at RFR’s 300 Atlantic St. in Stamford, CT. The transaction accommodates Rhone’s continuing growth of its established national brand presence, with more than 150 employees expected to occupy the new headquarters space. Founded locally in Fairfield County by brothers Nate and Ben Checketts in 2014, Rhone continues to expand its business. Rhone’s lease includes the top two floors of 300 Atlantic. “We are pleased to partner with Rhone for their new base of operations at 300 Atlantic,” said AJ Camhi, EVP and director of leasing of RFR. “Rhone’s principles and best-in-class product mesh perfectly with the RFR brand. We are thrilled that we could collaborate with the Rhone team on how to achieve their goals for this headquarters space to support their success.” Christian Bangert of Newmark represented Rhone. RFR’s Camhi, JoAnn McGrath and Rob Weller alongside a Newmark team of James Ritman, Brian Carcarterra, and Ben Goldstein represented RFR. The post Rhone Signs 40K-SF Headquarters Lease with RFR in Stamford appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Rhone (performance apparel) leases 40K SF headquarters at RFR's 300 Atlantic St., Stamford, CT
150+ employees; top two floors; founded Fairfield County 2014; continuing growth
Corporate office expansion; local Fairfield County brand scaling headquarters footprint
stories.summary: Performance apparel brand Rhone has leased 40,000 square feet of office space at RFR's 300 Atlantic Street in Stamford, Connecticut, accommodating more than 150 employees. Founded in 2014 by brothers Nate and Ben Checketts, Rhone is a Fairfield County-based brand expanding its national presence. The lease occupies the top two floors of the building.
stories.impact: Modest demand signal for Stamford multifamily. Rhone's 150-person office consolidation and growth indicates job creation and talent retention in the Stamford market; however, office-market leasing alone does not directly drive residential demand unless accompanied by significant in-migration or wage growth that attracts renters. Monitor for workforce expansion announcements that would signal apartment absorption strength in Connecticut's urban core.

stories.title: Asian-American Deli Café Hestia Signs 8K-SF Lease at 570 Lexington Avenue
stories.excerpt: A cafe serving Asian and American cuisine is opening a fourth Manhattan location, Commercial Observer has learned. Café Hestia, a group of family-run delis, has signed a 20-year, 8,000-square-foot lease at the base of the Feil Organization’s 570 Lexington Avenue, which it will likely also use as a catering facility, according to tenant broker Kassin Sabbagh Realty (KSR). KSR did not immediately disclose the asking rent, but the average asking rent for the nearby retail corridor along Fifth Avenue from East 42nd to East 49th streets was $575 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Our strategy has remained focused on finding operators that create lasting value for our tenants and the surrounding neighborhood, and Café Hestia builds on that vision with its all-day dining concept and wide variety of offerings,” Jordan Goldblum, director of retail leasing at the Feil Organization, said in a statement. Goldblum and Randall Briskin negotiated on behalf of the landlord in-house, while KSR’s Albert Manopla and Jack Khaski handled the deal for Café Hestia. KSR did not immediately provide a comment. Café Hestia’s other Manhattan locations are at 686 Third Avenue by Grand Central Terminal, 513 Seventh Avenue near Pennsylvania Station, and 80 Maiden Lane in the Financial District. Other tenants in the 50-story landmarked skyscraper on Lexington Avenue, also known as the General Electric Building, include international litigation firm Wolf Popper, which signed a 13,400-square-foot lease in December 2025, as well as the Real Estate Board of New York, which has a 23,031-square-foot office. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Café Hestia signs 20-year, 8K SF lease at Feil Organization's 570 Lexington Ave., Manhattan
Asian-American deli café fourth Manhattan location; ground-floor retail + catering use
Midtown retail corridor ask ~$575/SF (E. 42nd-49th, Fifth Ave. corridor, Q2 2026)
stories.summary: Café Hestia, a family-run Asian-American deli café, has signed a 20-year, 8,000-square-foot lease at the base of Feil Organization's 570 Lexington Avenue. This is the group's fourth Manhattan location; the space will serve as both retail and catering facility. Average asking rent for the nearby Fifth Avenue retail corridor (East 42nd to East 49th Streets) stood at $575 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Retail leasing in Midtown Manhattan indicates neighborhood foot traffic and mixed-use vibrancy but does not directly signal residential demand drivers or supply constraints. High asking rents ($575/SF) reflect strong retail market but do not correlate to apartment market fundamentals.

stories.title: Edgewood Capital Provides $28M Refi for Fort Lauderdale Condo Project
stories.excerpt: Latitude Group has landed a $27.9 million loan to refinance a newly completed condominium project in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. Edgewood Capital supplied the loan for the Terraces condo tower set to debut this fall, sources familiar with the deal told CO. Latitude Group previously secured a $24.5 million construction loan from Linkvest Capital in June 2024 to build the 22-unit development at 527 Orton Avenue, The Real Deal reported at the time. BayBridge Real Estate Capital arranged the refi with a team consisting of AJ Felberbaum, Jay Miller, Spencer Miller and Noah Rothman. Latitude acquired the half-ace development site for the project in 2020 for $3.3 million, according to TRD, citing property records. Sixty percent of the condos at the Terraces have been sold, according to the property’s website. The property’s amenities include a fitness center, a yoga studio, a swimming pool, cabanas and a community kitchen. Edgewood Capital, Latitude Group and BayBridge Real Estate Capital did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Edgewood Capital finances $27.9M refi for Latitude Group's condo project, Fort Lauderdale Beach
22-unit Terraces condo tower, 527 Orton Avenue; 60% pre-sales; fall 2025 delivery
Construction loan $24.5M (June 2024); acquisition price $3.3M (2020)
stories.summary: Latitude Group secured a $27.9 million refinance loan from Edgewood Capital for the Terraces, a newly completed 22-unit condominium project at 527 Orton Avenue in Fort Lauderdale Beach, debuting fall 2025. The project, which previously received a $24.5 million construction loan in June 2024, has pre-sold 60 percent of units. Latitude acquired the half-acre site in 2020 for $3.3 million.
stories.impact: Moderate signal for Fort Lauderdale condo and rental markets. 60% pre-sales and quick refi indicate strong local demand and lender confidence in South Florida coastal market; however, this is small-unit condo development, not multifamily rental. Refinancing availability and unit velocity suggest capital fluidity in the beach submarket but does not directly inform apartment supply or rental demand dynamics.

stories.title: Decron Properties Buys 163-Unit Property in L.A.’s Miracle Mile for $114M
stories.excerpt: Decron Properties has acquired a 163-unit property in Los Angeles’ Miracle Mile for $114 million as the firm’s first L.A. deal in nearly two years. The Los Angeles-based investment firm acquired the asset at 5550 Wilshire Boulevard, a residential and retail property developed in 2010, at what Decron described as a substantial discount to replacement cost. After focusing on Sun Belt markets, the firm said it continues to pursue opportunities across Los Angeles, San Jose, Orange County, San Diego and Seattle as well. “Our growth-market strategy has never been a referendum on Los Angeles,” Decron President and CEO David Nagel said in a statement. “For a period, the risk-adjusted returns here simply weren’t competitive with what we were finding in the Sun Belt markets.” Nagel added that Los Angeles remains “one of the nation’s most important and chronically undersupplied housing markets,” where new supply is difficult and expensive to build. 5550 Wilshire includes one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments and townhomes. Amenities include a pool and spa, a resident lounge, a private movie theater and rooftop lounges. The property also includes 14,686 square feet of ground-floor retail that is fully leased to tenants that include Chipotle, Five Guys and FedEx Office. JLL’s Blake Rogers represented both Decron and the seller in the transaction. Decron owns and manages nearly 10,000 multifamily units and about 1 million square feet of retail across California, Washington and Arizona, with a portfolio totaling roughly 8.7 million square feet. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Decron Properties acquires 163-unit property at 5550 Wilshire Boulevard, Miracle Mile, LA, $114M
2010-built asset; 1-, 2-, 3-BR units; ground-floor retail; purchased at discount to replacement cost
Decron's first LA deal in ~2 years; firm returning to CA markets after Sun Belt focus
stories.summary: Decron Properties acquired a 163-unit residential and retail property at 5550 Wilshire Boulevard in Los Angeles' Miracle Mile for $114 million, the firm's first LA deal in nearly two years. Built in 2010, the asset features a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom apartments and ground-floor retail, purchased at a substantial discount to replacement cost. Decron noted LA remains "chronically undersupplied" despite prior Sun Belt focus.
stories.impact: Strong signal for LA multifamily market, especially Miracle Mile submarket. Institutional buyer's return to LA after Sun Belt arbitrage saturation signals cap rates and risk-adjusted returns have normalized attractively; "substantial discount to replacement cost" suggests acquisition pricing below new construction, signaling limited new supply and entitlements barriers in LA. This telegraphs tighter market; developer should prioritize LA site control and approvals before cap rate compression narrows further.

stories.title: Corebridge Financial Refis Meatpacking Office Property With $293M Loan
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate has sealed a $293 million loan to refinance a mixed-use asset in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District, according to a release. Corebridge Financial provided the fixed-rate, permanent loan on the 158,957-square-foot building at 40 10th Avenue. The 2019-built property features 112,241 square feet of office space and 46,176 square feet of retail on the first two floors. Walker & Dunlop negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Dustin Stolly, Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre. “40 10th Avenue stands out in building quality, location and experience — all elements that differentiate a property for tenants,” Stolly, senior managing director of the capital markets institutional advisory team at Walker & Dunlop, said in a statement. “The fully leased office component, institutional tenant roster and substantial outdoor space demonstrate the continued demand for high-touch, well-located workplaces in New York.” The 10-story building has office tenants that include Starwood Capital Group, WestCap Management, RTW Investments, Stripes and Checkout.com. The retail portion of the property is occupied by Hyundai Motor. The property is positioned for success, according to Walker & Dunlop, since the Meatpacking District is one of Manhattan’s most supply-constrained office and retail submarkets. Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate landed a $150 million loan from Deutsche Pfandbriefbank in June 2020 to refinance construction debt to build the property, CO first reported at the time. Corebridge Financial, Aurora Capital and William Gottlieb Real Estate did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Aurora Capital / William Gottlieb JV refis 40 10th Ave., Meatpacking, Manhattan with $293M (Corebridge)
158,957 SF mixed-use: 112K SF office (fully leased), 46K SF retail, 2019-built
Fixed-rate permanent debt; strong tenant roster and outdoor space drive institutional demand
stories.summary: Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate secured a $293 million fixed-rate permanent loan from Corebridge Financial to refinance 40 10th Avenue, a 158,957-square-foot mixed-use property in Manhattan's Meatpacking District. Built in 2019, the property features 112,241 square feet of fully leased office space and 46,176 square feet of ground-floor retail. Strong institutional tenant roster and substantial outdoor space underpin demand.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office and retail refinancing in Meatpacking reflects capital availability and demand for mixed-use assets, but does not directly address residential supply, apartment demand, or rental market dynamics. Office component is fully leased, indicating stable institutional tenancy but no signal of residential conversion or multifamily appetite in the neighborhood.

stories.title: Stroller Brand Uppababy Relocates Store to 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights
stories.excerpt: Known for its distinctive strollers, baby gear brand Uppababy is relocating its store within Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The high-end baby accessories brand is opening a 3,780-square-foot brick-and-mortar location at Owen Realty’s 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, according to broker JLL. Uppababy will move next year from 90 Smith Street in Cobble Hill, where it established its Brooklyn retail and service “hub” in about 2019. JLL did not immediately provide the length of the lease or the asking rent for the space, but the average retail asking rent along nearby Fulton Street was $190 per square foot in 2025, according to the most recent retail report from the Real Estate Board of New York. “Brooklyn is an important market for Uppababy, and this relocation allows us to build on the relationships we have developed with local families,” Bob Monahan, co-founder and CEO of Uppababy, said in a statement. “Brooklyn Heights has a strong community of young and growing families, and the Montague Street location gives us the space and accessibility to deliver the hands-on product experience and personalized service that define our hub stores.” Uppababy manufactures and sells strollers, car seats, highchairs and other products for infants. Its top-of-the-line Vista V3 stroller, described on the company’s website as a “best seller,” retails for $1,000. JLL’s Jesse Wolff and Elijah Mehl represented the tenant in the transaction while Ryan Condren and George Danut, also from JLL, negotiated on behalf of Owen Realty. Owen Realty, which uses the LLC Montague Realty Development Associates, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “Montague Street offers the neighborhood density, visibility and accessibility that work well for family focused retailers like Uppababy,” Wolff said in a statement. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Uppababy (premium baby gear brand) relocates store to 156 Montague St., Brooklyn Heights, 3,780 SF
Moves from 90 Smith St., Cobble Hill (since ~2019); 2025 opening
Brooklyn Heights strong family demographic; Fulton St. retail corridor ~$190/SF (2025)
stories.summary: Uppababy, a high-end baby accessories brand, is relocating its Brooklyn retail and service hub to a 3,780-square-foot location at 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, opening in 2025. The firm is moving from 90 Smith Street in Cobble Hill, where it established its Brooklyn location around 2019. Brooklyn Heights' strong community of young and growing families attracted the brand to the Montague Street location.
stories.impact: Moderate signal for Brooklyn Heights multifamily demand. Uppababy's relocation to Brooklyn Heights—explicitly citing strong local family demographics—validates neighborhood household formation and young-family tenant base; premium positioning suggests affluent renter profile. Retail leasing activity on Montague Street indicates foot traffic and mixed-use vitality, supporting downstream apartment demand. Monitor for additional family-oriented retail/services (schools, pediatrics, childcare) as corroborating signals for family rental demand in this submarket.
